newsitem.title: USA: CNA to buy stake in Centre Financial.
newsitem.headline: CNA to buy stake in Centre Financial.

text.p: CNA Financial Corp said on Wednesday it has agreed to buy a majority stake in Centre Financial Products Ltd and will form it into a new risk securitization firm to be called Hedge Inc.
The new firm will be headed by Richard Sandor, chairman of Centre Financial and one of the founders of U.S. financial futures, CNA chief executive Dennis Chookaszian said.

Chookaszian told Reuters CNA has reached an agreement in principle with Centre Financial and said he expects the deal to close shortly. He declined to disclose the terms of the transaction, saying they were still under discussion.
Sandor founded Centre Financial Products in 1993 in association with Bermuda-based reinsurer Centre Reinsurance Co, a subsidiary of Zurich Insurance Co.

New York-based Center Financial's main business has been to develop products that focus on the intersection between the capital markets and the insurance industry, such as financial futures used to hedge a company's catastrophic or pollution exposures.
Chookaszian said the focus of Hedge Inc's business will be on developing such risk securitization products for CNA's use in property catastrophe and crop insurance.
Hedge Inc also may develop products for use in CNA's surety business as well, Chookaszian said, speaking to Reuters after the Insurance Leadership Forum in New York.
Chookaszian said Hedge Inc initially will focus on developing products for CNA's business but may expand its services to other insurers over time as the risk securitization market develops.
"We are going to try to be part of this new business," Chookaszian told the conference, sponsored by nine industry trade groups.
Other insurers such as American International Group Inc and General Re Corp have also begun focusing on the risk securitization business.
Risk securitization, or the transfer of insurance risk to the capital markets, has not had much success so far, with only a few small deals completed.
But Chookaszian said he believes the capital markets will play a larger role in risk transfer in the years to come.
Hedge Inc will have a staff of about 25 people, Chookaszian said.
